minutes.headline: Committee heard a field-fee dispute, kept the seasonal fee unchanged, and approved a pilot of eighth-grade Chromebooks.
minutes.summary: The meeting opened with a parent's complaint about being refused a ticket to his daughter's sports banquet. The committee approved the extended day handbook and an eighth-grade one-to-one Chromebook pilot, reviewed a draft capital plan, and heard the new superintendent's entry plan. A long discussion covered a youth football group's unpaid and unpermitted field use, and the committee reaffirmed the flat seasonal facility fee without a formal vote. It ended in executive session on contract strategy.

public_comment.topic: Was refused a ticket to his daughter's lacrosse banquet and asks the committee to address it; says he will keep coming back.

votes.motion: Approve the extended day program update and handbook changes
Accept the Chromebook one-to-one initiative for eighth grade as a pilot for the school year
Motion on policy/committee assignment (Jim Levesque) to revert to prior arrangement
Maintain the seasonal facility fee through fiscal year 2020 (no change); discussion concluded no vote was needed since not an agenda item
Enter executive session under MGL c.30A s.21(a)(2) for contract negotiation strategy with non-union personnel, not to return to public session

budget_items.what_was_said: Eleven open purchase orders were reviewed; the business manager said they are normal year-end carryovers and will be closed out.
A member asked about one open order; it was explained the invoice came in lower than the original estimate.
Town counsel advised the program cannot charge parents the extra staffing cost for a one-on-one aide, so the program absorbs it at the base rate.
Adding a grade to the one-to-one program affects the device replacement schedule and IT demand, so it is a pilot to test the budget impact.

budget_items.topic: Draft capital plan FY20-29: phone system
budget_items.what_was_said: Primary school phone replacement project was completed.
The abatement project was funded and a state source was found that may replace the capital expenditure.
Remaining hallway, stairwell and classroom work estimated as a large project.
Design and construction are scheduled in later years; the estimate may be high compared with a recent benchmark.

budget_items.topic: FY24 roof project and MSBA share
budget_items.what_was_said: A roughly million-dollar roof project would be MSBA-assisted with the town share around half.
Boiler replacement shown as a separate project; green community grant funds might offset it.
figures_as_heard: a quarter of a million dollars

budget_items.what_was_said: The reduced fee offered was rejected by the group, whose budget was lower; further cuts in access were offered.
figures_as_heard: four thousand nine hundred ninety dollars

budget_items.topic: Revolving account and unpaid lacrosse invoice
budget_items.what_was_said: The fee reduction was to be covered from the facility revolving account using new revenue, but a lacrosse invoice from spring remains unpaid.
A member noted part of the bond payment comes from the cell tower lease and part from facility user groups, so missing revenue must be made up.
The superintendent recommended no change to the seasonal fee through next year so groups can budget.

decisions.decision: Extended day director to return to update the committee in November.
Committee agreed to reaffirm, without a vote, that the flat seasonal facility fee stays unchanged, and to put it in writing on the website.
Superintendent to research stipended field-monitor positions in other districts and come back with a proposal.
Committee will wait to hear from the football association before acting.
Committee assignments (policy review) reverted to the earlier arrangement.

what_happened.line: The committee reaffirmed, without a vote, that the flat seasonal facility fee stays unchanged and is to be put in writing on the website.
After a long discussion of a youth football group's unpaid and unpermitted field use, the committee agreed to wait to hear from the association before acting.
The superintendent is to research stipended field-monitor positions in other districts and return with a proposal.
The committee took up an eighth-grade one-to-one Chromebook initiative as a pilot for the school year, partly to test the budget impact.
The extended day handbook update was taken up, and the director is to return in November; the draft FY20-29 capital plan was reviewed without a vote.

why_it_matters: Field fees for youth sports groups stay flat, and an unpaid invoice and a revolving account that depends on new revenue show how field upkeep is paid for outside the regular school budget.
The Chromebook pilot adds a grade to the device replacement schedule, so the pilot's results could shape future technology costs.
The draft capital plan lists building projects such as asbestos abatement, air conditioning, a roof and boilers, which would be paid for by the town budget, mostly taxes, with state help.
